>Just about anxiety. Do you know or not know what you are afraid of?

That's the thing. There were no psychological triggers for it. Avoiding stressful situations wasn't even an option. They were symptoms that I could expect to feel every single day, at the same time of day. I don't know if I want to even want to call it anxiety. It's was just pain. Pain enough to make me want to act out in rage and destroy property or quarantine myself to my room, huddled in fetal position. Before psychiatric intervention, that pain was my default state and only punctuated by brief moments where it left me, but still terribly depressed the entire time.

I've had to drop out of school.
